newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Swedish Riksbank to leave repo unchanged.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Swedish Riksbank to leave repo unchanged.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, will leave its key interest rate, the repo rate, unchanged at 4.10 percent at its weekly operation on Tuesday, a Reuter poll of 11 economists found on Monday.
The volatile and weak crown was the main reason most economists cited for keeping the repo rate steady at the 0730 GMT tender.
However some economists also said the scenario was affected by spiralling growth and an end to monetary policy easing in Europe.
"The Riksbank will not lower the repo tomorrow. There will be more cuts provided the crown strengthens and stabilises," said Peter Lindquist, HSBC Midland economist.
"But you can also expect no move until some time after the budget on April 15 because the Riksbank does not want to put its mark on politics."
Six of the 11 economists surveyed said there was still room for the repo rate to be lowered further.
Last year the repo rate, which is the bank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity was cut 25 times to the current level of 4.10 percent from 8.91 percent.
The other five economists were convinced the bank has lowered the repo as far as it will and the next move will be upwards.

"The repo rate has presumably bottomed. Growth has got more intense and monetary policy is already rather expansive on the grounds of the weak crown," said Stephanie Pfeiffer, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The Riksbank last lowered the repo rate on December 17 when it trimmed 25 basis points from the rate.
Its other key rates, the deposit and lending rates, stand at 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent respectively.

Economists interviewed for the poll were from Carnegie, Consensus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Hagstromer & Qviberg, Handelsbanken, HSBC Midland, PaineWebber, Paribas, Salomon Brothers, Swedbank and Ohman.
